threads.title: The Welkynd Census
threads.secret: Ayleid lamp-wardens tuned their light-stones into one continental instrument. A scholars' cabal from the Summerset libraries, calling itself the Lampwrights, is relighting the dead stones in order. When the last is lit, the Crystal Tower's lens will show the sky as it was before the fall, and wake the name-vaults.

entry.text: A scholar's census slate leans against the gate-arch: eight stone-names in a column, five struck through in a fresh hand. The last line reads, in Aldmeri: 'Then the Tower.'

quest.title: The Welkynd Census
quest.desc: A census slate at an Alessian gate lists eight light-stones, five of them struck through in a fresh hand.
quest.desc2: The lamps are being relit across the Cyrodiil ruins, the Valenwood vaults and the Tower of the Summerset Isles.
quest.pitch: A scholar at an old gate says someone is taking a census of the Ayleid lamps, and crossing them off.
quest.outro: I lit the eighth stone with my own hand. The Tower's lens turned slowly and, for the span of a breath, the sky above Summerset showed every star a thousand years gone. The Lampwrights bowed. I did not know what I had begun.

gate_of_alma_ruma.lead: Read the census slate at the Gate of Alma Ruma and head for the Shardiuss dig.
gate_of_alma_ruma.clue: a census slate with five of eight stone-names struck through

shardiuss_excavation.lead: Find the first relit lamp in the Shardiuss pit and follow the cabal's route west.
shardiuss_excavation.clue: a lamp relit in the pit, its flame a cold new white

note.x: Stone one: relit, Shardiuss. Stone two: Miscarcand's cold vault, relit by the third night. Stone three: Ne Salas pillar, pending. The cabal's instruction: light in order, do not skip. The order matters. Do not ask why; we have asked, and the answer was a silence like a held breath.

miscarcand.lead: Relight the Miscarcand name-lamp and carry its flame to the Valenwood towers.
miscarcand.clue: a lamp-gate relit with the cabal's cold white flame

note.x: To Aelwyn at the Tower. Two stones lit and the vault at Miscarcand is awake: do not let the Warden count the names while the lamps are new. I have left a seal on the lintel. We proceed to Ne Salas. The dead are listening; keep your voice level.

ne_salas.lead: Relight the Ne Salas pillar and take the cabal's tally on to the star-vault.
ne_salas.clue: a central pillar warm to the hand with an unfamiliar white

note.x: Ne Salas: the pillar relit at the fourth bell. A tone rose from it that no instrument could name. The cabal agrees that the stones are one voice and that we have only the third note of nine. We go to the Reliquary, then to the ashes. Say nothing to the Order.

reliquary_of_stars.lead: Relight the star-vault's ceiling and follow the white flame to the burned city.
reliquary_of_stars.clue: ceiling stars re-lit in a pattern that points southwest

note.x: The ceiling is a chart, not a sky. Four stars lit, thirty to go, and the vault answers with niches opening. We read one scroll: it was a list of the lamps themselves, nine in all, ending at a place called the Tower of Ten Thousand Years. I think we have been told where to go.

city_of_ash.lead: Relight the burned city's cistern lamp and sail for the Crystal Tower.
city_of_ash.clue: a cistern lamp relit in a field of ash

note.x: The City of Ash was the worst. I lit the lamp and every ash-figure on the terraces turned its head. One said a word. I have not repeated it since. The cabal's youngest has gone pale. We have one stone left and a Tower to face. I would give a great deal for a quieter instrument to play.

crystal_tower_summerset.lead: Climb the Crystal Tower to the lens-room where the last stone waits.
crystal_tower_summerset.clue: a lens-room whose lenses face the sky at the wrong angle

note.x: The ninth stone is the Tower's lens. When it is lit, the sky will show as it was. Be ready. The Ayleid names in the vaults below will rise, and the Psijic wardens will not be pleased. Do not let anyone near the lens-lever. It is not a thing that can be taken back.

psijic_relic_vaults.lead: Face the Lampwright Magister in the vaults beneath the Tower.
psijic_relic_vaults.clue: a vault door open for the first time in a thousand years

note.x: THE NINTH LAMP BURNS NOT FOR LIGHT BUT FOR REMEMBRANCE. Those who tend it tend the dead. Those who extinguish it forget the dead. Those who keep it must be willing to hear, in the dark, all that was done in the light.

threads.title: The Ash Remembers
threads.secret: Ash from Red Mountain carries a faint memory of the people it burned. A Telvanni theory holds that the memory seeds where it falls, in groves, in marshes and in the dreams of exiles, and that a Hist-tree in the south is the only thing that can read it all.

entry.text: A glass urn at a ghostfence gate-post holds a pinch of grey ash and a card: 'Falls where it chooses. Remembers what it burned. Follow the fall.' A map of the prevailing winds is pinned beneath.

quest.title: The Ash Remembers
quest.desc: A glass urn at the ghostfence holds a pinch of ash and a card: 'Falls where it chooses. Remembers what it burned.'
quest.desc2: The wind's trail runs from the volcano through a refugee canal and an island grove to the roots of the Hist.
quest.pitch: A Telvanni scholar insists that ash is a kind of speech, and that it has begun to say something.
quest.outro: The great Hist-root took the ashes into itself and, for an hour, I heard every name they had been. The ash will fall again, but it will fall quieter now. It has been heard.

ghostfence_morrowind.lead: Take the ash-urn and the wind-map from the ghostfence toward the volcano's crater.
ghostfence_morrowind.clue: an ash-urn pinned with a map of prevailing winds

note.x: I have measured the fall for nine years. The ash falls where there are people with something to forget: a city of refugees, a mining colony, a village that fled. It is not random. It is drawn. If you wish to know what the volcano is saying, follow the wind and listen to what the ash does when it lands.

red_mountain.lead: Gather a pinch of ash at the crater lip and follow the fall east.
red_mountain.clue: ash that drifts against the wind toward a distant canal

cheydinhal.lead: Visit the Dunmer refugees of Cheydinhal and learn what their ash-jars hold.
cheydinhal.clue: refugees' ash-jars labelled with ancestors' names

raven_rock.lead: Hear the ash-yam farmers of Raven Rock describe what the fallen ash says.
raven_rock.clue: grey ash-drifts that settle only on the north side of the bulwark

brodir_grove.lead: Walk the grove at dusk and listen to the ash in the roots.
brodir_grove.clue: grove-roots that whisper where ash has settled

note.x: Do not walk the grove at dusk. The ash settles on the roots and the roots begin to speak: a mutter, not a word. It is the volcano's own mutter, carried across the sea. Folk who linger hear their own dead. I have heard mine. Do not linger.

helstrom.lead: Cross the border at Helstrom and follow the ash into the fen.
helstrom.clue: a border-post whose ash-drifts always cross in one direction

thorn.lead: Ask the Hist-sages of Thorn to read the ash in the Great Pool.
thorn.clue: a pool whose surface takes ash and holds a ghost of it

note.x: Root of the marsh, drink what the wind brings. The ashes are not enemies, they are travellers, and they carry names. Let them rest in the sap and be heard. Let the dead of the north be known to the Hist, who forgets nothing and forgives all, and keeps each name against the dark.

root_whisper_village.lead: Lay the gathered ashes at the roots of the abandoned village and listen.
root_whisper_village.clue: a root-chair where ash has settled in the shape of a person

note.x: ~From the red hill to the green,~from the mountain to the mire,~ash goes drifting, ash is seen,~ash goes carrying its fire.~What it burned it will not lose.~What it knew it will not choose.~In the root, the ash is heard,~each name a quiet, rooted word.

threads.title: The Dwemer Dial
threads.secret: Each Dwemer ruin keeps a bronze dial in its deepest hall, all set to the same figure and all turning forward since the Heart was silenced. At the end of its sweep, the spire at Rkuldumz will answer. The dials were a countdown to a return, or a recall.

entry.text: A lever behind a stilled conveyor drops a bronze plate. Its face is a dial with one hand, its figure scratched with a tiny cross and, in scholar's script: 'Eight of these. All the same figure. All ticking.'

quest.title: The Dwemer Dial
quest.desc: A bronze dial behind a stilled conveyor, one hand, one cross, and the note: 'Eight of these, all ticking.'
quest.desc2: The dials are scattered across Morrowind, Solstheim, High Rock, Hammerfell and Elsweyr, and all answer to a spire on a rock.
quest.pitch: A scholar in the fabrication hall says there are eight dials, and that they have never been wrong.
quest.outro: At the spire's summit I held the last dial's hand an inch from its mark. The brass at my feet hummed, the brass in a hundred ruins hummed. I did not let it fall. I do not know what would have come, but I knew it would have been very old.

halls_of_fabrication.lead: Read the first dial in the Halls of Fabrication and note its figure.
halls_of_fabrication.clue: a bronze dial behind a conveyor, its hand one tick from the cross

arkngthand.lead: Find Arkngthand's dial above the centrifuge and compare its figure.
arkngthand.clue: a dial plate set beside the centrifuge seat

note.x: Dial two: Arkngthand, centrifuge side. Same figure as the first, same hand, same tick. I was told the dials were calibrated to local time. They are not. They are calibrated to each other. One hand moves, they all move. One dial stops, they all stop. This is a signal, not a clock.

nchardak.lead: Take the dial from Nchardak's coolant hall before the ice takes it.
nchardak.clue: a dial iced over but its hand still moving

kagrumez.lead: Read the Kagrumez dial under the star-dome and match its tick.
kagrumez.clue: a dial in the star-dome that ticks in time with the other seven

mthartzel.lead: Unfasten the Mthartzel dial from the pump hall's gauge-wall.
mthartzel.clue: a dial in a pump hall set to a gauge's wrong figure

note.x: DIAL SIX. PRESSURE: NIL. TIME: UNTIL. The pump is no longer the first concern of this hall. The hall exists for the dial. If the dial reaches its mark, every pump will cease at once and every door will open. Let it reach its mark. Let us be recalled.

volenfell.lead: Dig the Volenfell dial out of its sand-drift.
volenfell.clue: a dial half in a sand-drift, its hand still ticking

note.x: Found under a dune, a bronze plate with a hand that moves. I did not touch it. It ticked all night. At dawn a second hand appeared on the same dial, thin as a hair, and began to move faster. I do not like it. I have covered it with a goat-skin. I have asked a priest. He said it is not a prayer.

halls_of_colossus.lead: Find the dial beneath the colossus's chest and note how far it has turned.
halls_of_colossus.clue: a dial in the colossus's chest that has turned nearly full circle

note.x: The seventh dial is under the great machine's ribs. It has turned three-quarters. It is the nearest to its mark of any I have seen. The colossus is a clock-weight for it. Whatever will come, it will come when the dial and the colossus agree. I have left the dial alone, and I have left the colossus alone, and I have left.

rkuldumz_spire.lead: Reach the spire's summit and hold the last dial before it reaches its mark.
rkuldumz_spire.clue: a summit dial whose hand is a finger's breadth from the cross

note.x: ALL DIALS ANSWER HERE. When the eighth hand meets its mark the spire speaks, and all the halls of the world awaken at once. This may be a recall or a release. The dial does not distinguish. Hold the hand or let it fall. Choose carefully, hearer.

threads.title: The Sugar Road
threads.secret: A hidden counting-house buys the debts of every sugar farm, caravan and dockside inn from the Elsweyr coast to the Bitter Coast. Its patron is a pale lender who collects years of labour rather than gold, and keeps his strongbox on the stilts of a swamp market.

entry.text: A sugar-urn at the meadow's edge holds a debt-slip folded around a coin. The slip bears a watermark: a crescent moon and a ledger. 'Purchased. Do not pay the farmer. Pay the Counting-House.'

quest.title: The Sugar Road
quest.desc: A debt-slip in a sugar-urn with a crescent-and-ledger watermark: 'Do not pay the farmer. Pay the Counting-House.'
quest.desc2: The slips' trail runs from sugar farms and Khajiit caravans through river and lake towns to a stilt-market in the Bitter Coast.
quest.pitch: A farmer says her debts were bought by a house she has never met, and that its slips bear a moon.
quest.outro: The strongbox rose out of the mud on its chain, heavy with years instead of gold. I opened it, and I read the names, and I burned the slips one by one. I do not know how many were freed. I know I burned them all.

moon_sugar_meadow.lead: Take the debt-slip from the meadow's urn to the sugar farm that owes it.
moon_sugar_meadow.clue: an urn holding a debt-slip with a crescent-and-ledger watermark

note.x: The bearer of this slip owes, to the Counting-House of the Crescent Ledger, thirty-one years of labour at the rate of one year per hundred weight of sugar. The debt is purchased from the farm of Tathara and transferred without notice. The bearer will continue to be paid in the farm's own coin, minus interest.

tathara_sugar_farm.lead: Trace the farm's purchased debt to the sugar-port's counting-room.
tathara_sugar_farm.clue: a farm ledger with three pages stamped by an unfamiliar seal

senchal.lead: Open the Counting-House's branch behind a Senchal sugar warehouse.
senchal.clue: a warehouse wall with a ledger-and-moon plate screwed to it

baandari_caravan_stop.lead: Take the caravan-mother's debt-slips to the next town on the trade-road.
baandari_caravan_stop.clue: a tent of caravan-slips all stamped with the same watermark

note.x: Caravans in debt: forty-six. Debts held by the Crescent Ledger: forty-one. We have always paid the Counting-House with a cut of the sugar and a season's labour of the young. Nobody has seen the lender. Nobody wishes to. It is said he sleeps by day and by night and pays his debts in years.

rawlkha.lead: Follow the debt-slips from Rawlkha's lantern market north into Cyrodiil.
rawlkha.clue: a lantern-market stall that sells only paper

bravil.lead: Trace the Crescent Ledger's river-agents in Bravil's flooded cellars.
bravil.clue: a cellar where the ledger-and-moon seal is carved in a lintel

lunar_fang_docks.lead: Take the ledger's night-boats from the Lunar Fang Docks toward Morrowind.
lunar_fang_docks.clue: moonlamps painted with a crescent, a ledger on the lamp-post

note.x: Night boats from the Lunar Fang dock to carry sealed ledgers to the Bitter Coast. No questions. No passengers. If a passenger is found aboard, the passenger is to be delivered to the master at the swamp-market, who will see that no harm comes to them. We pay in years.

balmora.lead: Break the Counting-House's silt-strider ledger-room in Balmora.
balmora.clue: a silt-strider cargo-hold stamped with a ledger

gnaar_mok.lead: Open the strongbox beneath the Gnaar Mok stilts and face the Pale Lender.
gnaar_mok.clue: a stilt-house whose floor is a hatch with a ledger on its lid

note.x: THE CRESCENT LEDGER KEEPS ITS DEBTORS. THE DEBTORS KEEP THEIR YEARS. If you open this box you will know each name on it, and each name owes you. Be a creditor or a liberator. The swamp does not tell you which is easier.

threads.title: The Bone Census
threads.secret: Every ancient dragon grave on Tamriel and Akavir is missing one vertebra. The Tsaesci serpent-court has been collecting them to build a spine, a ladder to somewhere high, and its agents have visited every barrow and mound in the last ten years.

entry.text: A great dragon's rib-arch with a gap in its spine: one vertebra, neatly removed, a clean saw-cut. A tag in a courtly hand: 'Number 14 of 41. Inspected. Collected.'

quest.title: The Bone Census
quest.desc: A dragon's rib-arch with one vertebra neatly removed and a courtly tag: 'Number 14 of 41. Collected.'
quest.desc2: The missing bones trace from desert and mountain graves to an ice mound and a valley of ribs, and on to a serpent temple.
quest.pitch: A bone-picker says every dragon grave he knows is missing a single piece, taken cleanly and tagged.
quest.outro: In the serpent temple a spine of forty-one vertebrae lay in a cradle, two short of its full length. I took the one I had carried and laid it down, but not in its place. The court's ladder will remain forty-one rungs; it will not reach.

prowls_edge_dragonscour.lead: Read the tag on the dragonscour's missing vertebra and find the next grave.
prowls_edge_dragonscour.clue: a rib-arch with a clean saw-cut gap and a numbered tag

sancre_tor.lead: Search the Akaviri barrow for the next tagged bone-niche.
sancre_tor.clue: a barrow's dragon-bone niche empty, its tag still in place

note.x: Bone nineteen of forty-one: taken from the Sancre Tor barrow in the winter of last year. A Tsaesci in a monk's robe made the cut, courteous, and left a donation. I did not stop him; I did not know the count. Forty-one graves, forty-one bones. I do not know where the others are. I suspect the east.

hvitkald_peak.lead: Climb Hvitkald to the peak's cairn and read the tag left on a frozen rib.
hvitkald_peak.clue: a frozen rib on the summit with a numbered tag

onsis_breath.lead: Find the bone-arch's missing vertebra among the singing stones.
onsis_breath.clue: a singing arch with one vertebra replaced by a plain stone

note.x: Onsi's arches are dragon vertebrae. One is replaced by a pale stone, cut to fit, with a tag: 'Number 23.' Beneath the stone is a dry niche where the true bone was. Whoever took it left a good copy and a note of thanks. I would have preferred an apology. The wind sings through the gap in the wrong key.

the_frozen_dragon_mound.lead: Climb the frozen mound and find the bone the serpent-court could not take.
the_frozen_dragon_mound.clue: a frozen throat with a clean hole where a vertebra should be

note.x: A foreign man came to the mound last year in a cloak of red silk. He cut a bone from the dragon's throat while it slept, and the dragon, which had not stirred in a thousand years, shuddered. The ice began to crack that night. Do not let any who wear red silk near the mound.

dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.lead: Cross the valley of ribs and find the bone-marked cradle path to the temple.
dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.clue: a ribcage whose spine has a gap exactly one vertebra wide

temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.lead: Reach the temple's spine-cradle and decide where the forty-first bone goes.
temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.clue: a cradle of vertebrae two short of its full length

note.x: FORTY-ONE FOR THE LADDER, FORTY-ONE FOR THE CLIMB. When the last is set the court will rise. We have waited a thousand years. We can wait for two more bones, and a quiet that does not end.

threads.title: The Tide-Ledger
threads.secret: The last navigator of the Yokudan fleet tore his tide-ledger in nine and hid the pieces in nine ports across the seas, so no single people could chart the road home. The Maormer want the road; the Redguards want the route to a hidden isle of kings; the Altmer want to bury it again.

entry.text: A scale-mosaic tile at the temple's threshold bears an unfamiliar tide-glyph and a navigator's mark. Scratched into its edge: 'One of nine. Seek the other eight. Read at low tide only.'

quest.title: The Tide-Ledger
quest.desc: A scale-mosaic tile bears a navigator's tide-glyph: 'One of nine. Read at low tide only.'
quest.desc2: The ledger's nine pieces lie in ports from Hammerfell and Solstheim to the Maormer isles and Yokuda.
quest.pitch: A serpent-priest says the tile came from a ledger torn in nine, each piece hidden in a different sea.
quest.outro: In the sunken temple's hall I laid the ninth page against the other eight and a chart of tides unfolded across the water. The road home was shorter than I had feared, and stranger. I set the pages back, one in each of nine ports, so no one people would own the road.

temple_of_satakal.lead: Take the navigator's tile from the temple threshold to the Hammerfell harbour.
temple_of_satakal.clue: a threshold tile with a tide-glyph and a navigator's mark

port_hunding.lead: Find the harbour's hidden ledger-page behind its sealed manifest.
port_hunding.clue: a harbour cabinet containing a page marked with a tide-glyph

note.x: Page two of nine: hidden in the manifest cabinet at Port Hunding. It gives a tide-hour and a heading for the first stage. Hide it again. Do not carry it on the sea unless you have the others; a single page leads to a reef.

stros_mkai.lead: Read the lighthouse's treaty plate for a tide-glyph and carry it north.
stros_mkai.clue: a lighthouse plate with a tide-glyph hidden in its border

haknirs_shoal.lead: Pry open the wreck's bow-chest for a ledger page among the barnacles.
haknirs_shoal.clue: a bow-chest holding a salt-stained page with a tide-glyph

firsthold.lead: Search Firsthold's lighthouse for the fourth page, hidden in its lens-case.
firsthold.clue: a lens-case with a page folded under the glass

serpent_pens.lead: Take the fifth page from the keeper's totem and look for the Maormer's copy.
serpent_pens.clue: a keeper's totem with a page rolled into its hollow

note.x: To the admiral: a page of the Yokudan ledger has come into my keeping. It was in the totem's hollow. I am told it is the fifth of nine. I do not know what it is for. It seems to be tides. If it is valuable, I would like an honest price. If it is dangerous, I would like it taken away.

orgnums_citadel.lead: Consult the sea-king's window for the sixth page and the Maormer's secret.
orgnums_citadel.clue: a throne-hall window with a page pasted behind its glass

note.x: THE SIXTH PAGE LOOKS ON THE DEEP. The sea-king keeps it where his gaze may rest upon it. He says it is a map to a place he does not wish to visit. If you take it, he will know. If you do not, he will wonder, and wondering is how kingdoms fall.

ra_gada_encampment.lead: Bring the gathered pages to the Ra Gada drill-master and ask his counsel.
ra_gada_encampment.clue: a drill-post with a ledger page nailed beneath its crossbar

note.x: A seventh page, nailed under the lesson-post by a hand I did not see. I have no wish to read it. It is the property of the kings, not the camp. The final two pages lie beyond the water, in a place where the kings sleep. If you mean to read the ledger, you must first complete the Last Lesson.

sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.lead: Lay the nine pages on the funeral barge and read the ledger's tide.
sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.clue: a funeral barge with nine page-shaped hollows in its deck

note.x: NINE PAGES, NINE PORTS, NINE HANDS. The road home is not a place but a tide, and it comes but once in each age. Read it aloud and the barge will sail. Burn it, and the kings will sleep. The tide does not care which you choose.

threads.title: The Sundered Crown
threads.secret: A conqueror known by a dozen names, remembered by every people as a foreign king, was buried in eight pieces under eight realms' royal tombs so he could not rise. Someone is gathering the regalia, a finger-ring in a barrow, a crown in a ship, a throne-arm in the ice, to make him whole.

entry.text: A king's tomb has a seal cut cleanly in two, the other half missing. Beside it is a fresh chisel-mark and a note: 'Number three. The ring is gone. The ring of the Hollow King.'

quest.title: The Sundered Crown
quest.desc: A royal tomb's seal cut in two, with a note: 'Number three. The ring is gone. The ring of the Hollow King.'
quest.desc2: The pieces of the Hollow King lie in barrows, throne-halls, ships and ice from High Rock to Akavir.
quest.pitch: A grave-warden says someone has been taking pieces of royal regalia from tombs, one realm at a time.
quest.outro: At the ice throne I found the last piece already in the thief's hands: a woman in a pilgrim's cloak who wept as she held the crown. She had never wanted him whole. She wanted him found. I helped her bury him again, deeper.

tomb_of_lost_kings.lead: Examine the cut seal in the lost kings' tomb and follow the thief south.
tomb_of_lost_kings.clue: a royal seal cut in two, the other half missing

tuwhaccas_throne.lead: Look for the missing throne-arm inscription in the desert king's hall.
tuwhaccas_throne.clue: a throne with an arm sawn clean away

note.x: The east arm of the throne was cut away in the dry season by a thief who left the sword and the ring and took only this. The arm bore a name in a script I have not seen anywhere else. I copied it before the arm was taken. It reads: HOLLOW. I do not know what else. I am afraid to say it twice.

tomb_of_the_apostates.lead: Search the hollow tree's heartwood for the missing tomb-panel.
tomb_of_the_apostates.clue: a heartwood panel prised out, the cut still weeping sap

note.x: One panel gone from the heartwood: a carving of a crowned figure with its face hollowed out. The tree is not a tomb for the Pact's dead; it was a tomb for something older, planted over it to keep it quiet. The apostates' chant, I now suspect, was never to the great walker. It was to the thing in the heartwood.

soulrest.lead: Ask the island keepers of Soulrest which crypt was opened last.
soulrest.clue: a crypt-door unlocked with a key-shaped scar in its lintel

note.x: Crypts opened this decade: one. Name: unlisted. Contents removed: a circlet of grey metal, unadorned. The crypt was never inscribed. We did not know who lay in it, only that the lilies grew in the shape of a crown above it. We left the lilies. The thief took the circlet and left the lilies. The thief asked for nothing.

old_orsinium.lead: Descend into Old Orsinium and find the hammer-forged piece in the lowest forge.
old_orsinium.clue: an anvil with a ring-shaped scorch in its face

note.x: THE THIRD SMITH BROKE THE CROWN. The fourth smith broke the sword. The fifth smith did not break the ring, for she could not; she buried it in the forge, and the forge forgot. Let no hand lift it, for a ring lifted is a ring that remembers its finger.

gyldenhul_barrow.lead: Examine the barrow's mural for the missing finger of the ancient king.
gyldenhul_barrow.clue: a mural king with one finger scraped away

wolf_jarls_howe.lead: Climb into the howe's ship and find the crown in its keel-chest.
wolf_jarls_howe.clue: a keel-chest with its lock sprung and its lid ajar

note.x: To my heirs: I have the crown of the foreign king beneath the keel of my ship and I will carry it to my own grave rather than let it go to any living man. It is a heavy thing. It weighs nothing. It does not shine. I will not look at it. Bury me on top of it, and do not ask why my sleep is so poor.

frost_throne_of_kamal.lead: Reach the ice throne and face whoever has gathered the Hollow King.
frost_throne_of_kamal.clue: a throne-arm with a socket shaped like a ring

note.x: THE EIGHTH PIECE SITS HERE: THE ARM THAT HELD THE SCEPTRE. He who sets the ring, the crown, the sceptre and the sword in their places makes the king whole, and the king will rise, and the king will remember who he was. There is no one left who remembers who he was. This is the mercy.

threads.title: The Silent Falls
threads.secret: The continent's great waterfalls and cascades are falling silent one night at a time, each hush a verse of a binding lullaby. A coven of water-witches is singing the Weeping One, a buried wamasu fossil under the Black Marsh falls, into a sleep it will never wake from, and the world's tears with it.

entry.text: A pilgrim's notebook left on a flat rock: eight falls named, six crossed out with the date and a single word, 'hushed'. 'Tonight: the pool at Mist Mirror. Do not be near the water when it stops.'

quest.title: The Silent Falls
quest.desc: A pilgrim's notebook names eight waterfalls, six crossed out as 'hushed', and warns that tonight is the pool at Mist Mirror.
quest.desc2: The hush has moved from falls and aqueducts to a lava-cascade, a weeping inn, an ice seam and finally to the Black Marsh falls.
quest.pitch: A pilgrim says the waterfalls are falling silent in order, one a night, and nobody can stop it.
quest.outro: I stood in the spray of the last falls as the water dropped to a whisper and the wamasu in the rock began to weep. The coven's eighth verse was unfinished. I sang the other eight from memory, in the old tongue. The water remembered its voice.

mist_mirror_refuge.lead: Read the pilgrim's notebook at the pool and follow the hush north-east.
mist_mirror_refuge.clue: a pool whose waterfall stops at midnight and starts at dawn

waterdancer_falls.lead: Stand at the base of Waterdancer Falls when the water falls silent.
waterdancer_falls.clue: a waterfall whose spray rainbow flickers on the hour

note.x: Do not stand at the base at midnight. The water stops, and you will hear a woman singing a lullaby in the old tongue. It is very gentle. It is not for you. Every fall is a verse and every verse a drowsier one. I do not know who she is singing to. I know that I will not be here when it is finished.

tor_hame_khard.lead: Wait at the waterfall court of Tor Hame Khard for the hush.
tor_hame_khard.clue: a waterfall court whose cascade is silent for one hour each night

anequina_aqueduct.lead: Sit beneath the aqueduct's arches on the night the channel stops.
anequina_aqueduct.clue: an aqueduct channel that falls silent, its stones humming a lullaby

note.x: The channel went quiet at the second bell. Not dry: quiet. The water stood still in its bed and a note came from the stones, a lullaby, a hum that I felt in my teeth. I tried to cry out and found I could not. At dawn I was lying in the channel with my cheek on the wet stone, and my face was wet with tears.

molag_mar.lead: Visit the lava-cascade's grotto at Molag Mar the night it falls silent.
molag_mar.clue: a lava-cascade that cools and stills at the hush hour

weeping_giant.lead: Sit beside the weeping giant's cheek and listen as the tears slow.
weeping_giant.clue: a giant's cheek whose tears slow to a single drop a minute

note.x: The tears stopped last night. The first time in a hundred and thirteen days. I sat with the cup beneath the cheek and waited, and none came, and I wept myself. I do not know why I wept. There was a lullaby in the wind and I did not recognise the tongue. It was the gentlest thing I ever heard. I did not want it to stop.

stalhrim_source.lead: Visit the stalhrim basin at the hush and note the hum's pitch.
stalhrim_source.clue: a stalhrim hum that drops a tone at the hush hour

weeping_wamasu_falls.lead: Climb to the weeping falls and face the coven before the last verse.
weeping_wamasu_falls.clue: a falls whose note has thinned to a whisper

note.t: The Lullaby of the Last Water
note.x: ~Hush, little river, the night is long.~Hush, little spring, I will sing you a song.~Hush, little fall, the tears are deep.~Hush, great mother, and go to sleep.~The world has wept enough, they say.~Close your eyes, and fade away.
